### 1. [HIGH] command-injection-os-system
- Tool: semgrep | Rule: `python.django.security.injection.command.command-injection-os-system.command-injection-os-system`

- Why it matters: Request data detected in os.system. This could be vulnerable to a command injection and should be avoided. If this must be done, use the 'subprocess' module instead and pass the arguments as a list. See https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Command_Injection for more information.

### 2. [HIGH] sqlalchemy-execute-raw-query
- Tool: semgrep | Rule: `python.sqlalchemy.security.sqlalchemy-execute-raw-query.sqlalchemy-execute-raw-query`
- Location: /tmp/vuln/app.py:9
- Why it matters: Avoiding SQL string concatenation: untrusted input concatenated with raw SQL query can result in SQL Injection. In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.
- Recommended fix: Review the flagged code path and apply the rule's recommended secure pattern (validate input, use parameterized APIs).

### 3. [HIGH] tainted-sql-string
- Tool: semgrep | Rule: `python.django.security.injection.tainted-sql-string.tainted-sql-string`
- Location: /tmp/vuln/app.py:9
- Why it matters: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.
- Recommended fix: Review the flagged code path and apply the rule's recommended secure pattern (validate input, use parameterized APIs).
